facts.text: The package registers Gymnasium environment Turtlebot4Env-v0 with entry point tb4_drl_navigation.envs.diffdrive.turtlebot4:Turtlebot4Env and max_episode_steps=500.
Turtlebot4Env defines a two-element float32 Box action space with low [0.0, -1.0] and high [1.0, 1.0].

Turtlebot4Env defines a Dict observation space with min_ranges and min_ranges_angle shaped by num_bins and bounded by the scan range and angle, dist_to_goal bounded 0.0 to 100.0, orient_to_goal bounded -pi to pi, and the last action copied from the action space.
step stores the action, converts action[0] to the linear.x twist component and action[1] to angular.z, publishes the twist through Publisher, and propagates the state for time_delta seconds.
Sensors creates a sensor_msgs/LaserScan subscription on /scan and a nav_msgs/Odometry subscription on /odometry/filtered.
Publisher creates a TwistStamped publisher on /cmd_vel with queue depth 10.
pub_cmd_vel stamps the TwistStamped with the node clock and the configured base frame and publishes it.
reset passes seed to Gymnasium's super().reset(seed=seed), calls SimulationControl.reset_world(), zeroes the last action and republishes it, and reads start_pos/goal_pos from options.
SimulationControl creates a ControlWorld service client on /world/<world_name>/control.
SimulationControl.reset_world requests a ControlWorld reset with model_only=True, and pause_unpause sets world_control.pause to the requested value.
_propagate_state unpauses the world, spins the executor until time_delta elapses, pauses the world, and then reads the observation from the sensors.
When reset options omit start_pos and goal_pos, the start and goal yaws are drawn from np.random.uniform(-pi, pi), not from the seeded Gymnasium RNG.
The environment terminates when dist_to_goal < goal_threshold or min(min_ranges) < collision_threshold.
README states that Gazebo Sim does not support model reset and that the robot's odometry and pose are reset with the SetPose and SetEntityPose services.
The tutorial says num_bins creates 30 bins by default and can be as high as len(ranges).

determinism.notes: The analytic fake stores the reset seed and returns fixed placeholder observations; the seed does not reproduce the upstream ROS 2/Gazebo scenario.

fidelity.engine: analytic:analytic fake (no ROS 2, Gazebo or physics)
gaps: the fake is a ROS-free analytic stand-in: it creates no ROS 2 nodes and never contacts /scan, /odometry/filtered, /cmd_vel or the Gazebo /world/<world_name>/control service
all observation values, rewards and terminal flags are placeholders; the fake applies no TurtleBot4 dynamics, contacts, lidar, odometry or reward logic

the fake reports 30 lidar bins, the upstream constructor default (docs/Tutorial.md:42); the live length is the LaserScan ranges length and num_bins is clamped to it (turtlebot4.py:260), so the real observation array size is not fixed by the clone
the action space is copied from the upstream environment (turtlebot4.py:187-191); the fake does not publish a TwistStamped on /cmd_vel and does not advance Gazebo for time_delta
the upstream reset samples the scenario with ScenarioGenerator(seed=None) and np.random.uniform; the fake's seed only selects its placeholder distance
the registered max_episode_steps=500 TimeLimit wrapper is not applied to the fake; only the bridge's ticks and max_steps bounds apply
rendering, observation images, TF, snapshots and the full LaserScan array are NOT COVERED

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: The simulated environment is held at its last observation: the runtime refuses further world steps until an operator reset. The latch does not publish a zero Twist on /cmd_vel and does not stop a mobile base subscribed to that topic.
